sector_model: nonfinancial (electronic trading marketplace; fee based, no balance sheet lending)
thesis: Tradeweb is a high margin (GAAP operating margin about 43% in Q3), debt free electronic bond and derivatives marketplace with 2.1B cash, revenue +14.9% and ADV +22.4% in Q3 2026. At about 28.7x TTM total net income and 3.7% FCF yield it is priced as a quality compounder, not as cheap; quality is clear but price attractiveness is unestablished.
counterthesis: Volumes depend on rate volatility and credit issuance (Q3 benefited from rate and central bank uncertainty); fees per million fell about 10% in rates derivatives and cash credit on mix; Q3 market data revenue was lifted by LSEG contract delivery timing; the 1.97B Trumid deal (1.89B cash, close 1H 2027) is the largest ever and would absorb most cash and bring integration risk; LSEG and banks remain large holders; a 23% rise from the Q3 buyback average of 103.83 leaves little margin of safety; tax receivable agreement liability 317M.
invalidation: ADV growth turning negative for two quarters, revenue growth below 8%, adjusted EBITDA margin below 50%, Trumid closing at materially higher price or with credit volume share loss, or loss of LSEG market data contract.
